The occupation census raised reconstructed households for the trades a town of 3,265 people needed and could not document; `justice_of_the_peace` was not one of them, which is why this person could only ever be ADDED and never seated on an existing record — data/research/newspapers/register_1835.json calls it `new_resident` for exactly that reason. A scan read that confirms or corrects the name upgrades this entry. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 2 times, as “WALKER JAMES”, 1830-10-04: 2 lots in the platted town — lot 4 of block 10 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L4BL10CHIOT, as printed); lot 4 of block 19 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L4BL19CHIOT, as printed), 0.00 acres stated in all, for $56.00 (ls1528, ls1529). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $56.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. This one argues for a PERSON: the Democrat and the American name James Walker as a justice of the peace at Chicago 1 time(s), and this reconstruction did not hold them. `data/residents/` has no way to carry a person except inside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing: one member, no dwelling, no division, no origin, no arrival beyond the bound the paper sets.
